entry.title: Journey Through Java - Day 2: The Origin Story of Java - From Oak to OpenJDK
entry.summary: Welcome back to Journey Through Java! Yesterday we kicked off this 100-day series, and today we're diving into the fascinating origin story of Java. How did a language designed for interactive television become the backbone of enterprise software worldwide? Back in June 1991, Java wasn't even called Java. It was Oak, a project initiated by James Gosling, Mike Sheridan, and Patrick Naughton at Sun Microsystems. The original vision? Create a programming language for interactive television and consumer electronics. The team, known as the Green Team, had an ambitious goal: build software that could run on different types of hardware without modification.
